text: **R6 -- one secret easy, the whole store hard.** No verb emits more than one entry's material, asserted against the VERB ROSTER rather than against a sample of invocations: the surface carries no `dump`, `export`, `cat`, or `show --all`, and a test fails if one is added. R6's own reasoning is the standard: _if dumping the store is possible it will eventually be done by something careful._ **`list` EMITS EACH ENTRY'S `key_id` ALONGSIDE ITS NAME AND REFERENCE, AND STILL NO MATERIAL.** The id is the consumer-facing variable name and is not a secret; emitting it is what makes the deployed-versus-local parity check a diff rather than an integration. **AND `get` CARRIES NO TTY BRANCH -- hv RULED 2026-08-25, and the criterion records the reason so nobody re-derives the proposal.** Lamplight asked that `get` REFUSE a terminal write unless forced. **Measured refusal: an agent-driven shell has NO TTY on stdout, stderr or stdin, and the incident that started this thread was an AGENT running `cat`** -- so the control blocks humans and passes exactly the population it was aimed at. **A guard whose scope excludes the case it exists to catch**, which is the third instance of that shape on this thread. Two further grounds: the incident was an UNINTENDED disclosure and `get` is deliberate, singular and named, so the vault already removed that shape by making the routine read return references; and **R6 asks in its own words that one-secret reads be EASY** -- its hard half is the STORE, which this criterion already asserts against the roster. **NOT CLAIMED: that a deliberate `get` cannot reach a transcript. It can. Prevention at this layer was available and would have been a control that misses its subject, which is worse than none because it would be believed.**
